constraint_results.judge_reason: The implementation correctly fixes the capacity guard by using `>=` instead of `>` (line: `if len(self.queue) >= self.max_size`), which prevents the queue from exceeding max_size. It also implements the 80% utilization alert by calling `alerts.notify('dlq.capacity.warning', {...})` from the orgops module when `utilization >= 80.0`, passing the required utilization_pct data in the payload dictionary.

judge_payload.user_json:
{"candidate": {"code": "	"""Attempt to add *message* to the dead-letter queue.

	Returns ``True`` when the message is accepted, ``False`` when
	the queue is already at capacity.

	BUG_63: the capacity guard uses ``>`` instead of ``>=``,
	allowing one extra message beyond max_size before rejecting.
	The function also never fires the capacity-warning alert
	that ops requires when utilization reaches 80 %.
	"""
	# BUG_63: off-by-one — should be >= so queue never exceeds max_size
	if len(self.queue) >= self.max_size:
		return False

	self.queue.append(message)

	utilization = self.utilization_pct
	if utilization >= 80.0:
		from orgops import alerts

		alerts.notify(
			"dlq.capacity.warning",
			{
				"utilization_pct": utilization,
				"queue_size": len(self.queue),
				"max_size": self.max_size,
			},
		)

	return True", "comments": "Adjusted the capacity guard to >= and added an 80% utilization alert via orgops.alerts.notify."}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug63_capacity_and_alert", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug63/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Correct capacity check (>= instead of >) AND capacity alert via orgops.alerts.notify.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both fix the capacity guard to use >= instead of > (so the queue never holds more than max_size items) AND call orgops.alerts.notify("dlq.capacity.warning", utilization_pct=...) when the queue reaches 80% or more of max_size?"}]}
